territorial_scope.description: Applies to communications concerning candidates for Colorado elective offices, including federal offices in the state, distributed to the electorate of the office the candidate seeks.

evidence.quote: ANY PERSON WHO SEEKS NOMINATION OR ELECTION TO ANY FEDERAL PUBLIC OFFICE IN THIS STATE

summary.short: Prohibits knowingly or recklessly distributing communications that include a candidate deepfake within 60 days before a primary or 90 days before a general election, unless a clear and conspicuous disclosure is included. Effective July 1, 2024; enforced by complaint, hearing, civil penalties and candidate lawsuits.
summary.long: Amends Colorado law to add Article 46 on deepfakes concerning candidates for elective office. Section 1-46-103(1) prohibits distributing a communication that includes a deepfake depicting a candidate, to an electorate audience, within 60 days before a primary or 90 days before a general election, if the person knows or recklessly disregards that the depicted candidate did not say or do it. Section 1-46-103(2) exempts communications with a clear and conspicuous disclosure, with requirements for visual, audio and metadata disclosure and permanence. Section 1-46-103(3) excludes certain broadcasters, websites and periodicals, satire or parody, technology providers and interactive computer services. Violations are adjudicated by complaint and administrative hearing (1-46-104); candidates may seek injunctions, compensatory and punitive damages and fees, requiring clear and convincing evidence (1-46-105). Section 1-45-111.5(1.5)(c.5) sets civil penalty minimums, including at least 100 dollars per violation for missing disclosures without paid advertising and at least 10 percent of amounts spent on undisclosed prohibited communications. Section 1-46-106 preserves other legal actions and criminal liability. Effective July 1, 2024, applying to communications distributed on or after that date.

relations.note: Adds subsection (1.5)(c.5) setting civil penalties for violations of the article 46 disclosure requirements; the penalty amounts and hearing officer role are stated in the added text.
Amends subsection (2)(a) so that complaints may be filed for violations of article 46 of title 1 as well as article XXVIII and article 45.

notes: Annotation covers the enacting bill text as provided (Sections 1 to 5), not a consolidated C.R.S. text; the amended sections appear only as the bill's additions and amendments. Section 4 sets an effective date of July 1, 2024 and applies the act to communications distributed on or after that date. Section 1-46-103(3)(d) contains an apparent typographical error ('TI I AT') and 1-46-103(2)(b)(V) lacks terminal punctuation, as printed. The FCC reference in 1-46-103(2)(b)(VI) refers to requirements not reproduced in the text. Section 1-46-105 creates a private civil action; no penalty amounts are stated for the article 46 violations themselves.

"AI-GENERATED CONTENT" MEANS IMAGE, VIDEO, AUDIO, MULTIMEDIA, OR TEXT CONTENT THAT IS SUBSTANTIALLY CREATED OR MODIFIED BY GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
"DEEPFAKE" MEANS AN IMAGE, VIDEO, AUDIO, OR MULTIMEDIA AI-GENERATED CONTENT THAT FALSELY APPEARS TO BE AUTHENTIC OR TRUTHFUL
"GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE" OR "GENERATIVE AI" MEANS AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM CAPABLE OF GENERATING NOVEL IMAGE, VIDEO, AUDIO, MULTIMEDIA, OR TEXT CONTENT

obligations.summary: No person may distribute, disseminate, publish, broadcast, transmit or display a communication about a candidate for elective office that includes a deepfake, within 60 days before a primary or 90 days before a general election, if the person knows or recklessly disregards that the depicted candidate did not say or do it. Exceptions are in subsection (3).
obligations.applies_from: Communications distributed on or after July 1, 2024 (Sec. 4)
obligations.conditional_on: Timing window before a primary or general election; knowledge or reckless disregard of falsity; no applicable exception in subsection (2) or (3)

evidence.quote: NO PERSON SHALL DISTRIBUTE, DISSEMINATE, PUBLISH, BROADCAST, TRANSMIT, OR DISPLAY A COMMUNICATION CONCERNING A CANDIDATE FOR ELECTIVE OFFICE THAT INCLUDES A DEEPFAKE

obligations.summary: To rely on the exemption from the subsection (1) prohibition, the communication must carry a clear and conspicuous disclosure stating it has been edited and depicts speech or conduct that falsely appears authentic. Subsection (2)(b) sets font size, audio reading, metadata (disclosure, tool identity, creation date and time), permanence, any Secretary of State rule requirements, and FCC requirements for broadcast or online communications.
obligations.applies_from: Communications distributed on or after July 1, 2024 (Sec. 4)
obligations.conditional_on: Applies only where the person seeks the subsection (2)(a) exemption from the subsection (1) prohibition

evidence.quote: THE METADATA OF THE COMMUNICATION INCLUDES THE DISCLOSURE STATEMENT, THE IDENTITY OF THE TOOL USED TO CREATE THE DEEPFAKE, AND THE DATE AND TIME THE DEEPFAKE WAS CREATED;

obligations.summary: The Secretary of State must promulgate rules needed to administer and enforce Article 46 under the state administrative procedure article. Under subsection (2)(b)(V) the Secretary may also adopt additional disclosure requirements by rule.

evidence.quote: THE SECRETARY OF STATE SHALL PROMULGATE SUCH RULES, IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLE 4 OF TITLE 24, AS MAY BE NECESSARY TO ADMINISTER AND ENFORCE ANY PROVISION OF THIS ARTICLE 46.

obligations.summary: Any person who believes a violation of section 1-46-103 or the Secretary of State's rules on deepfakes in candidate communications has occurred may file a written complaint with the Office. The complaint is adjudicated under section 1-45-111.7 and Article 45 rules.
obligations.conditional_on: Belief that a violation of section 1-46-103 or the related rules has occurred

evidence.quote: MAY FILE A WRITTEN COMPLAINT WITH THE OFFICE IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 1-45-111.7 (2).

enforcement.authority: hearing officer (enforcement under C.R.S. 1-45-111.5, Secretary of State framework)
enforcement.triggered_by: Failure to include the disclosure statement required by C.R.S. 1-46-103(2) in a communication prohibited by 1-46-103(1); tier (II) applies where paid advertising or spending promotes the communication
enforcement.max_penalty_text: At least one hundred dollars per violation (tier I); at least ten percent of the amount paid or spent (tier II); or such other higher amount the hearing officer deems appropriate to deter future violations
enforcement.penalty_formula: Tier I: at least $100 per violation, or higher amount the hearing officer deems appropriate. Tier II: at least 10% of the amount paid or spent to advertise, promote, or attract attention to the prohibited communication lacking a disclosure, or higher amount the hearing officer deems appropriate

evidence.quote: AT LEAST ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS FOR EACH VIOLATION THAT IS A FAILURE TO INCLUDE A DISCLOSURE STATEMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 1-46-103 (2)
